title: refactor(ci): consolidate lint/test/release workflows and bump Actions/Node versions
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: our repository has accumulated many overlapping GitHub Actions workflows for lint, test, and release automation. This has increased maintenance burden and caused inconsistent cache usage and longer CI times. This PR consolidates the workflows into a smaller set (lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml) with a shared reusable workflow for node-based steps, bumps GitHub Actions/checkout/setup-node versions, and standardizes cache keys and matrix configurations.

This is a behavioral-only refactor: no runtime code is changed. Goals: reduce CI config duplication, improve caching hit rate, enable faster PR feedback, and make future changes (node/action bumps) easier to apply across repositories.

Changes included (checklist):
- [x] Introduce .github/workflows/.lint.yml that calls .github/workflows/reusable/node-steps.yml
- [x] Introduce .github/workflows/.test.yml with consolidated matrix and cache keys
- [x] Replace multiple release workflows with a single release.yml using workflow_dispatch and repository_dispatch triggers
- [x] Bump actions/checkout to v4 and actions/setup-node to v4, adjust caches for node 20 and 18 builders
- [x] Consolidate common steps into .github/workflows/reusable/node-steps.yml (checkout, setup-node, restore/save cache, install, run)
- [x] Add comments + docs in the workflows directory for maintainers

Notes:
- CI changes validated against redwood monorepo. Local dry-runs and workflow_dispatch tests performed. Some legacy repositories referencing old workflow filenames will be updated in a follow-up migration PR to avoid churn in external integrations.
- Follow-up: create a repo-automation job to apply similar patterns across SDK repos (redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript) once this pattern is approved (ENG-7124).

Commit summary:
- Consolidate: create reusable workflow and three entry workflows (lint/test/release)
- Infra: bump actions/checkout & setup-node; unify cache keys
- Docs: add CONTRIBUTING.md section with CI guidelines

Merge rationale: reduces duplication, improves CI performance, and centralizes action versions for future maintenance.
